title: The Paleobiology Database application programming interface
Denormalized occurrence and taxon tables of the Paleobiology Database
authors: The Paleobiology Database Community; Kocsis, Á.T.
datasetSnapshot: PBDB full taxon table downloaded 2026-07-19; pbdb_taxa_csv.zip MD5 fca5fde5e8d5922d06fe332a42b955f9

title: Open Tree of Life web services
note: Topology and taxonomy context; divergence dates require separate evidence.

title: Reassessing a cryptic history of early trilobite evolution
note: Primary phylogenetic and palaeobiogeographic reassessment; inferred topology and origin timing remain matrix- and model-conditioned.

title: Rapid volcanic ash entombment reveals the 3D anatomy of Cambrian trilobites
note: Primary X-ray microtomographic study of articulated Tatelt Formation trilobites; feeding and homology interpretations are separated from imaged anatomy.

title: The trilobite upper limb branch is a well-developed gill
authors: Hou, J.-B.; Hughes, N.C.; Hopkins, M.J.
note: Primary ESEM and micro-CT comparison of Triarthrus and Olenoides appendages; respiratory performance is a functional inference from preserved structures.

title: Uniquely preserved gut contents illuminate trilobite palaeophysiology
note: Primary synchrotron microtomographic inventory of the gut contents of one Bohemolichas specimen; diet and gut chemistry remain bounded inferences.

title: Burgess Shale fossils shed light on the agnostid problem
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
note: Primary description and phylogenetic analysis of mature Burgess Shale agnostinids; sister-group placement and ecology are sampled interpretations.

title: Urokodia sheds light on the origin of chelicerae and book gills of Chelicerata
note: Primary X-ray microtomographic redescription and phylogenetic analysis of Urokodia; appendage homology and stem placement remain analytical interpretations.

title: A chelicera-bearing arthropod reveals the Cambrian origin of chelicerates
note: Primary description of the KUMIP 314091 holotype and Bayesian/parsimony analyses; body-plan and trophic conclusions remain specimen- and matrix-bounded.

title: Neuroanatomy in a middle Cambrian mollisoniid and the ancestral nervous system organization of chelicerates
authors: Ortega-Hernández, J.; Lerosey-Aubril, R.; Losso, S.R.; Weaver, J.C.
note: Primary imaging and elemental mapping of Mollisonia nervous tissues; neuroanatomical and appendicular signals conflict and are not collapsed into one topology.

title: Giant claw reveals the largest ever arthropod
authors: Braddy, S.J.; Poschmann, M.; Tetlie, O.E.
note: Primary description of a 46-centimetre Jaekelopterus chelicera; total body length is an allometric estimate with explicit scaling assumptions.

title: The phylogeny and systematics of Xiphosura
note: Primary expanded morphological phylogenetic analysis; traditional synziphosurines are tested as a polyphyletic assemblage rather than assumed to be horseshoe crabs.

title: A Silurian ancestral scorpion with fossilised internal anatomy illustrating a pathway to arachnid terrestrialisation
note: Primary description of UWGM 2162 and 2163; pulmonary-cardiovascular homology and habitat remain interpretations constrained by preservation and nearshore deposition.

title: Increasing species sampling in chelicerate genomic-scale datasets provides support for monophyly of Acari and Arachnida
note: Primary phylogenomic analysis optimized against systematic error; support for Arachnida and Acari is dataset- and model-conditioned.

title: Arachnid monophyly: Morphological, palaeontological and molecular support for a single terrestrialization within Chelicerata
authors: Howard, R.J.; Puttick, M.N.; Edgecombe, G.D.; Lozano-Fernandez, J.
note: Primary 200-slow-gene analysis plus reanalyses and fossil/morphology synthesis; single terrestrialization is a topology-dependent historical inference.

title: Comprehensive species sampling and sophisticated algorithmic approaches refute the monophyly of Arachnida
note: Primary dense taxon phylogenomic and total-evidence analysis recovering Xiphosura within a paraphyletic Arachnida; competing model results remain explicit.

title: Lopingian (Late Permian) trilobites from the North Caucasus, Russia, with an overview of their distribution worldwide
note: Revises Changhsingian North Caucasus material and reviews other Lopingian trilobite occurrences; it constrains late sampled records without making every lineage persist to the boundary.

title: A middle Cambrian arthropod with chelicerae and proto-book gills
note: Primary anatomical and phylogenetic study of Mollisonia plenovenatrix. Its benthic-micropredator interpretation is species-bounded and is not transferred to the profiled M. symmetrica neural specimens.

title: Morphological and ontogenetic criteria for defining a trilobite species: The example of Siluro-Devonian Phacopidae
authors: Crônier, C.; Bignon, A.; François, A.
note: A phacopid case study within Phacopida; it is not an order-wide range analysis.

title: Trilobite systematics: the last 75 years
note: Reviews unresolved order-level classification, including the paraphyletic traditional Ptychopariida.

title: Cambrian–Ordovician trilobite family Missisquoiidae Hupé, 1955: Systematic revision and palaeogeographical considerations based on cladistic analysis
authors: Lee, S.-b.; Lee, D.-C.; Choi, D.K.
note: A family-level sample within Corynexochida, not a complete order history.

title: The oldest described eurypterid: a giant Middle Ordovician (Darriwilian) megalograptid from the Winneshiek Lagerstätte of Iowa
authors: Lamsdell, J.C.; Briggs, D.E.G.; Liu, H.P.; Witzke, B.J.; McKay, R.M.
note: The named Winneshiek material and sampled matrix provide a local minimum record, not a global eurypterid origin.

title: Phylogenomic Resolution of Sea Spider Diversification through Integration of Multiple Data Classes
authors: Ballesteros, J.A.; Setton, E.V.W.; Santibáñez-López, C.E.; Arango, C.P.; Brenneis, G.; Brix, S.; Corbett, K.F.; Cano-Sánchez, E.; Dandouch, M.; Dilly, G.F.; Eleaume, M.P.; Gainett, G.; Gallut, C.; McAtee, S.; McIntyre, L.; Moran, A.L.; Moran, R.; López-González, P.J.; Scholtz, G.; Williamson, C.; Woods, H.A.; Zehms, J.T.; Wheeler, W.C.; Sharma, P.P.
note: Broad living-family sampling resolves a sampled pycnogonid tree; it does not date the fossil origin.

title: Phylogenomic Interrogation of Arachnida Reveals Systemic Conflicts in Phylogenetic Signal
authors: Sharma, P.P.; Kaluziak, S.T.; Pérez-Porro, A.R.; González, V.L.; Hormiga, G.; Wheeler, W.C.; Giribet, G.
note: The study documents conflict among arachnid data partitions and does not establish an uncontested total-group topology.

title: The spider tree of life: phylogeny of Araneae based on target-gene analyses from an extensive taxon sampling
authors: Wheeler, W.C.; Coddington, J.A.; Crowley, L.M.; Dimitrov, D.; Goloboff, P.A.; Griswold, C.E.; Hormiga, G.; Prendini, L.; Ramírez, M.J.; Sierwald, P.; Almeida-Silva, L.; Álvarez-Padilla, F.; Arnedo, M.A.; Benavides Silva, L.R.; Benjamin, S.P.; Bond, J.E.; Grismado, C.J.; Hasan, E.; Hedin, M.; Izquierdo, M.A.; Labarque, F.M.; Ledford, J.; Lopardo, L.; Maddison, W.P.; Miller, J.A.; Piacentini, L.N.; Platnick, N.I.; Polotow, D.; Silva-Dávila, D.; Scharff, N.; Szűts, T.; Ubick, D.; Vink, C.; Wood, H.M.; Zhang, J.
note: An extensive sampled spider topology, not a fossil range or direct-ancestry result.

title: Mitochondrial Metagenomics Reveals the Ancient Origin and Phylodiversity of Soil Mites and Provides a Phylogeny of the Acari
authors: Arribas, P.; Andújar, C.; Moraza, M.L.; Linard, B.; Emerson, B.C.; Vogler, A.P.
note: Mitochondrial soil-mite sampling and model-based dates do not directly observe the origin of Acari.
